name: Lauki Chana Dal with Soy Tadka
ingredients: ½ cup (100 g) dry chana dal, rinsed and soaked 30 minutes
25 g dry soy granules, rehydrated and squeezed
1 tsp (5 ml) canola or mustard oil
Pinch of hing (check gluten-free label if needed)
½ tsp Kashmiri chilli powder, optional
steps: Soak chana dal for 30 minutes, then drain. Rehydrate soy granules in hot water for 8–10 minutes, drain and squeeze dry.
Add dal, turmeric and 2 cups fresh water to a pressure cooker. Cook until tender but still holding shape; timing varies by cooker and soak. Release pressure safely.
Heat measured oil in a separate pan. Add cumin and hing, then onion; soften with a splash of water rather than extra oil.
Add ginger, tomato, coriander and chilli powder. Cook until tomato softens.
Add diced lauki and cook covered 7–9 minutes until nearly tender.
Fold in cooked chana dal with some cooking liquid and soy granules. Simmer 5–7 minutes so flavours combine; add water for a spoonable consistency.
Finish with coriander and lemon. Taste before adding salt. Serve with a measured portion of whole-wheat roti and extra non-starchy vegetables.
note: Inspired by everyday lauki-chana dal. Soy granules add protein without relying on cream or ghee. Chana dal is both a protein and carbohydrate source; include its carbohydrate in meal planning. Approximate nutrition only; not a treatment for LDL or A1C.
